subject: spaceGalley
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: spaceship galley kitchen.
Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo.

spec.name: Nostromo Galley
spec.description: A cramped, greasy, lived-in 1979 Nostromo-style spaceship galley: fridge, prep counter with CRT, cooking range under a hood, a bolted mess table with stools and a cat, all in a beige-and-grey utilitarian shell with amber and fluorescent lights.
spec.layout: A corner of a working starship. Viewed from the front (+Z), looking at the back wall (z = -1.4 wall face). Along the back wall, left to right as the viewer sees it: the tall fridge/freezer block at x -1.8..-0.95 (the model's right), the prep counter with sink, CRT monitor and overhead cabinets at x -0.95..0.6, and the cooking range with extractor hood at x 0.6..1.8 (the model's left). A solid bulkhead wall stands on the model's left (x +1.8..+1.95, z -1.55..-0.1) with a hatch frame; the right side is open. The mess table, a bolted steel pedestal table 1.4 x 0.8 m with four round stools and a tabby cat, stands at floor centre-front (x ±1.25, z -0.1..1.3). Ceiling girders, ducts, pipes and strip lights hang from y 2.2..2.4, with no ceiling plate. The deck is a dark grey grated plate (y 0..0.08) with a yellow/black hazard edge at the front. Everything else rests on the deck top (y = 0.08). Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo. Truckers-in-space industrial, not sleek. Dirty cream and putty panels, dark grey and olive trim, stainless steel, rust-orange pipework, rivet rows, toggle switches, stencilled labels, amber warning lamps, a green phosphor CRT, strip fluorescents. Everything is boxy and blocky with chunky chamfered greebles and a lot of small bolted detail. Grime is built as small stain patches and scuff strips in the grease colour on lower faces and near the range. Glow (kits/glow) is used for lamps, strip lights, CRT and indicator lights only. Everything is static (no joints). Parts avoid each other's boxes; wall details of a part stay inside that part's x range. The shell owns the bare wall plane, and the zone parts mount their things in front of it at z > -1.39.

parts.builds: The room itself and its overhead and bulkhead details, at the footprint x ±1.95, z -1.55..1.55. DECK: a dark deck plate (deck) y 0..0.08 over the whole footprint; raised grating squares (deckGrate and deckLight) tiled in a regular grid with bolt heads at the corners; a hazard-stripe band (alternating hazardYellow and black angled blocks) along the front edge at z 1.4..1.55; a drain grate near x -0.5, z 0.9; grime stain patches and scuff strips at the foot of the counters and range. BACK WALL: panelCream slab x ±1.95, z -1.55..-1.4, y 0.08..2.4, as large panels with panelShade seam strips every 0.6 m and rows of tiny rivets along the seams; a darker panelDark skirting strip y 0.08..0.22; stencilled label plates (small black and hazardYellow rectangles, an svg text texture such as GALLEY or MESS) on a free wall area at the far right x -1.7..-1.0, y 2.1..2.25; vertical conduit runs and cable clips in the corner x -1.9. Leave the wall plain behind the zone parts. LEFT BULKHEAD: x 1.8..1.95, z -1.55..-0.1, height to 2.4, panelOlive with seam grid, a rounded-rectangle hatch frame (panelDark and steel) at z -1.0..-0.3, y 0.3..1.9 with a wheel-lock handle, hinge blocks and a small amber indicator lamp, rivet rows, a warnRed hand-lever box and a fire-extinguisher (red cylinder with black hose and steel bracket) near z -0.25, y 0.5..1.1. CEILING (no ceiling plate): two cross girders (panelDark, x-axis, at z -0.9 and z 0.9, y 2.2..2.4) with bolted flanges; a thick duct run (steel, box section) along x at y 2.3 with clamp bands, flanged joints and a vent grille; a bundle of three pipes (pipeCopper, rust and steel) along x at z -1.25, y 2.15..2.3 with coupling rings and valves with red handwheels; hanging black cable loops; four strip fluorescents (lampWhite glow, with panelDark housings) under the girders at y 2.18, z -0.4 and z 0.9, x ±0.8; two amber caged warning lamps on the ceiling near the bulkhead. The shell leaves free the zones above the counters (the overhead cabinets, y 1.45..2.25 over x -0.95..0.6) and the hood area (x 0.6..1.8, y 1.55..2.3, z > -1.38).
parts.attaches: Provides the deckTop (y 0.08), wallFace (z -1.4), ceilingUnderside (y 2.2) and bulkheadFace (x 1.8) that all other parts build to.

parts.builds: The tall fridge/freezer and a food-dispenser block at x -1.8..-0.95, z -1.4..-0.7, y 0.08..2.05. A steel-and-cream cabinet on a recessed panelDark plinth (y 0.08..0.2): upper freezer door and lower fridge door as separate slightly proud panels (panelCream with panelShade rims), each with a steel recessed bar handle on brackets, hinge blocks on the right edge, a latch on the left; a control strip at the top with 3 toggle switches (steel levers on black plates), two rotary knobs, a small amber indicator lamp (glow) and a green status LED (glow); a stencilled temperature label plate; bolt-head rows; a venting grille with louvres along the bottom; coolant pipes (pipeCopper) rising from the top into the ceiling at x -1.4 with insulation wraps (panelShade) and a pressure gauge (steel disc, black face, red needle); a tiny hazardYellow warning triangle and a frost/ice build-up as small ceramic-coloured blocks around the freezer door gasket (black rim); grime streaks and scuff marks near the bottom and near the handles; a magnetic-tab clipboard of paper (ceramic plate with black dash lines) hung on the front by a steel clip; a vertical food-ration dispenser (blueGrey box with a chute and a tray, 4 round push buttons in amber, red, ceramic and crtGreen) bolted on the cabinet's right side wall at z -0.9 (cabinet side x -1.8, bolt the box slightly proud). Dispenser built to stay inside the box.
parts.attaches: Stands on deckTop at fridgeCenter, back against wallFace; its right edge x -0.95 touches the prep counter; its pipes rise to ceilingUnderside.

parts.builds: The prep counter with sink, wall-mounted CRT monitor and overhead cabinets at x -0.95..0.6, z -1.4..-0.75, y 0.08..2.25. COUNTER: a panelOlive cabinet body y 0.08..0.9 on a dark plinth, with 4 drawer/door fronts (panelCream with steel pull handles, rivet corners, stencilled number plates) and a steel worktop (y 0.9..0.94, front edge lip slightly proud, rounded steel rim); a recessed sink at the mount sinkCenter (x -0.45): a dark-hole basin built as a ring of steel walls, a steel gooseneck tap (sweep) with two red/blue valve wheels, a drain plug, a draining rack with 3 plates and 2 mugs (ceramic, coffee inside); on the worktop to the right: a toaster/food heater (steel box with 2 slots, a dial and lever) , a coffee pot (steel base, black glass pot, coffee inside) on a hot plate with a glowing amber ring, a cutting board (olive-wood colour from grime/panelOlive) with a knife (steel blade, black handle) and a stack of 3 foil trays (steel), a cluster of cans with stencilled labels (rust, hazardYellow and panelCream bands), a spice rack of 5 little jars. WALL CRT at crtCenter (x 0.25, y 1.3, in front of wall): a swivel steel arm bracket, a boxy beige CRT housing with a chunky bezel (panelShade), glowing crtGreen screen with dark scanlines and text lines (svg texture, glow) such as a menu or MOTHER readout, brand plate, two knobs and a keyboard strip (panelDark with small key blocks) on a shelf below at y 1.1. OVERHEAD CABINETS at overheadCabinets (y 1.5..2.25, z -1.4..-1.05, x -0.9..0.55): 3 wall cabinets in panelCream with olive trim, steel handles, hinge blocks, one door slightly open? (no joints, so keep closed); under-cabinet strip light (lampWhite glow) with panelDark housing; grime/stain patches; a label plate each; a hanging steel ladle rack with 4 utensils under the cabinet between the sink and CRT at y 1.45 (hooks and tools). Backsplash between worktop and cabinets (x -0.95..0.6, y 0.94..1.5): steel plate with seam strips and rivets, grime splashes behind the sink.
parts.attaches: Stands on deckTop; back against wallFace; left edge x -0.95 touches the fridge, right edge x 0.6 touches the range; worktop at counterTop (y 0.92 / 0.94 top); cabinets stay below ceilingUnderside.

parts.builds: The cooking range, extractor hood and utensil rack at x 0.6..1.8, z -1.4..-0.7, y 0.08..2.3. RANGE BODY at rangeCenter: a steel-and-panelCream cabinet y 0.08..0.9 with panelDark plinth; front: a large oven door (steel frame, black glass window with a faint amber glow strip inside, a thick bar handle on brackets, a thermometer dial); below it a storage drawer with a pull handle; above the door a control panel (panelDark) with 4 big rotary knobs (steel with white indicator marks), 5 toggle switches, a timer dial and 3 small glowing indicator lights (red, amber, crtGreen); stencilled labels; rivet rows; grime and grease splatters thicker toward the top and around the oven door. COOKTOP at rangeTop (y 0.92): black enamel top with 4 round burners (concentric black and steel rings, small grate bars forming cross supports, a faint glowing amber ring on the front-left burner); a tall stainless stockpot with riveted handles and lid knob; a frying pan with long handle holding a few food discs (grime/coffee/catCream colours); a kettle; a steel spatula and ladle resting on a spoon rest; a small pile of tins/foil packs; a ring of small curling steam wisps? NO: skip steam. HOOD at hoodBase (y 1.55..2.3, z -1.4..-0.85): a trapezoid steel hood (box tapering), panelDark rim, a grease filter grille with louvres, two lamps underneath (amber glow in cages), a large chimney duct (steel, square) rising to ceilingUnderside y 2.2 and flanged, bolts, a red emergency stop button with hazardYellow guard and a small fire-suppression nozzle (rust/ steel cone) under the hood; a hanging utensil rail at y 1.45 on the wall with a ladle, whisk, tongs and a chopper (steel and black) between the hood and the prep counter side at x 0.62..1.0 wait: rail at x 0.7..1.7 just under the hood, over the backsplash (steel plate y 0.94..1.5 with seams and grease streaks). Side: a gas bottle (rust cylinder with steel valve and hazardYellow band) between range and the bulkhead is NOT used; instead a small pipe (steel) running from the range back into the wall. The range abuts the bulkhead at x 1.8.
parts.attaches: Stands on deckTop at rangeCenter, back against wallFace; left edge x 0.6 touches the prep counter, right edge x 1.8 touches the bulkheadFace; chimney meets ceilingUnderside; cooktop at rangeTop height 0.92 equals counterTop.

parts.builds: The crew mess table, stools, cat and tableware at x ±1.25, z -0.1..1.3, y 0.08..0.95. TABLE: a steel top 1.4 x 0.8 m (x ±0.7, z -0.05..0.75, y 0.74..0.78) with raised rim, rounded corners built from chamfer blocks, a panelDark underside frame, a single thick central pedestal (steel cylinder, flared base plate bolted to the deck with 4 bolts, a hazardYellow stripe ring near the foot); on the top: 4 place settings with stainless trays (steel, with 3 compartments and food blobs in catCream, grime and crtGreen-ish olive colours), forks/spoons, mugs (ceramic with coffee, one rust-coloured), a shared coffee flask (steel with black lid), a stack of ration packs (panelOlive with hazardYellow label), a salt/pepper pair, a small clipboard/log tablet, a crumpled napkin, a handheld communicator (panelDark with an amber light), grime rings and spill stains; a cat food bowl (ceramic with a blueGrey rim, half full) on the deck near the table's left pedestal side at x 0.5, z 0.95. STOOLS: four bolted swivel stools at the mounts stoolFrontLeft, stoolFrontRight, stoolSideLeft and stoolSideRight (round padded seat in blueGrey over a short panelDark ring, a steel single column, a flared base plate with bolts, a footrest ring), seat height 0.5, seats show seam stitching lines and wear patches in panelDark. JONES THE CAT: an orange tabby (catOrange with catCream chest and stripe bars in rust) sitting on the stool at stoolFrontRight (x -0.35, seat top y 0.55): built chunky from primitives (egg body, round head, two triangle ears with inner pink-cream, big eyes (black slit pupils on amber/crtGreen discs, glow not needed), tiny nose, whiskers, four paws, a curled tail wrapped around front), looking forward toward +Z, roughly 0.4 m tall.
parts.attaches: Stands on deckTop (y 0.08); table top at tableTop (y 0.78, centre z 0.35); stools at the stool mounts; stays in front of the counters (z > -0.1), clear of the hazard band at z > 1.4.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a static prop for a spaceship galley kitchen in the Nostromo style: lived-in, 1979 retro-futurism, grey-green panels, amber lights, CRTs, toggles, and clutter. I'm also weighing whether it needs any joints, though static looks fine so far, and I'm roughing out a corner footprint around 3.6 by 2.4 by 3.0.

I'm laying out the galley module now: a deck floor plate, a back wall with counters, and a roughly 3.6 by 2.4 by 3.0 footprint sitting on y=0. I'm weighing whether to leave the side wall open and tracking the grating, conduits, and ceiling lamp strips as separate boxes that can overlap the floor.

I'm deciding how to divide the shell into parts: a deck floor, a bare back wall, and a ceiling with ducts and lights. Each one sits in its own layer, with the back wall running along the rear of the footprint, and I'm working out how to keep the wall surfaces clear of mounted objects between the floor and the ceiling.

I'm dividing the galley's zones along the x-axis: the cooking range on one side, a prep counter with overhead cabinets in the centre, and cold storage with a wall dispenser on the other. The front centre is reserved for a dining table.

I'm settling the parts list now: a shell, a cooking station, a prep counter with overhead cabinets and a CRT, a cold storage unit, and a mess table, each with a rough triangle budget that keeps the total under 900.

I'm placing the fridge at the left end of the back wall, the prep counter in the middle, and the cooking range at the right, with the hood above the range. The overhead cabinets sit above the prep counter, and the mess table goes at the centre front.

I'm working out where the stools and table sit: the table top is about 1.5 by 0.8, centred toward the front, with stools on both sides and one at the front. I'm also weighing whether to add a low side wall on the open edge, and I'm leaning toward keeping just the back wall and ceiling, with the shell carrying floor grating, hazard stripes, conduits, and vents.

I'm settling the galley's dimensions: widening the footprint to about 3.9 by 2.4 by 3.1, with the back wall set a little forward and the counters running back to it. I'm also weighing a bulkhead on the left side with a hatch frame, and leaving the right side open.

I'm settling on a side wall along the left (+X) edge that runs back to a hatch frame, leaving the right side open, which lets the cooking range sit against that wall. I'm also deciding against a full ceiling panel so the view from above stays clear, and I'll rely on cross beams and pipes for the overhead structure.

I'm picking out the colour palette now: grey-greens, cream, rust, copper, and amber for the lamps, plus CRT greens for the screens.

I'm fixing the back-wall layout now: the mount points go in a dictionary, and the wall shell keeps clear of counters and overhead cabinets. Its vertical details stay within the backsplash band between the counters and the cabinets, so nothing collides at the seams.

Next I'm deciding how the shell's wall seams and panels meet the zone items: the shell keeps seams and rivets across the whole back wall, while the other parts sit in front of it on their own x ranges. I'm also considering whether ceiling strips and glow effects, maybe for the lamps and CRTs, can carry the steel look.

Still writing the box definitions...

Still settling the mess table and its stools: the table top is about 1.4 by 0.8 near the centre front, with stools at the sides and two at the front. I'm also budgeting the shell at around 170.

Still assigning the budgets for the cold storage, prep counter, cooking station, and mess table, then describing the shell's details: grating on the floor, yellow hazard stripes along the front edge, beige wall panels with seams and rivets, and a hatch frame on the left bulkhead.

I'm adding a cat, Jones the tabby, perched on the front-right stool beside the mess table, and I'll keep the bowl on the table as the main prop. Then I'm writing the whole layout up as JSON with the palette, mount points, and colour names spelled out.

I'm settling on the coordinate convention now: +X is the model's left side, so the bulkhead and cooking range sit on that edge.

I'm writing the buildColdStorage function that produces the fridge, keeping it fairly detailed but lean, with static parts attached straight to the root and no joints.

I'm settling the cabinet's footprint inside the box: the body narrows to make room for a thin dispenser on the right side, and the pipes will run up to 2.2 so they attach to the ceiling.

I'm laying out the fridge's body and doors: a plinth at the base, a body spanning the box's width up to just short of the counter, and the front doors split into a lower fridge section and an upper freezer section with a thin control strip at the top.

Still writing the door and handle details...

Still writing the fridge's helper functions and visual details.

Still writing the buildColdStorage details: the dispenser buttons sit on the outer face of the dispenser, and two copper pipes run up at the cabinet's back edge with insulation rings around them.

Still writing the cylinder placements and the gauge mount, with the pipes set at slightly different x positions.

I'm writing one function that builds the mess table part, aiming for an efficient but detailed build of up to about 160 parts. It'll be static with no joints, so each piece is placed with b.part at a set position, and since there are no joints there's no bone and the parts stay in model space. I'll use the Ctx type as the module already provides it, without declaring it myself.

I'm laying out the stools next: four of them at set spots around the table, each with a base plate, a column, a footrest ring, and a cushioned seat sitting within the deck bounds. The table top sits at the stated height with its pedestal and flared foot, and I'm adding a hazard ring near the base.

Still working out the cat on the stool: the body is an egg-shaped sphere sitting on the seat, with the head placed a little lower and the ears kept just under the top limit. The chest is a cream sphere on the front, the front paws are cylinders and the back haunches are spheres at the sides, and the curled tail is an arc of torus geometry.

Still laying out the cat's markings, eyes, nose, and ears, then the table's place settings: four trays with compartments and food, arranged around the top.

Still building out the table's details: the trays beside the settings, mugs, a flask at the centre, ration packs, salt and pepper, a tablet, a crumpled napkin, and a lit communicator. Then the grime rings and spills on the top, plus the frame with corner blocks at the rim.

Still working on the underside: the frame gets a panel-dark ring beneath the top and braces running to the pedestal. The rim goes on as thin strips with chamfered corner blocks, and I'm setting up a shared helper to place each part with its position and rotation.

Still working through the bowl placement: a bowl at the earlier spot would clash with the stool's base plate, so I'm shifting it outward along x to clear the stool.

Still counting the parts for the stools, which come to about 13 each, and checking the table build against the budget.

Still tallying the parts, now the table's own pieces: the top, rim and corner blocks, the frame, pedestal and flare, and the hazard ring, then the settings at about ten parts each. Trimming the stool bolts and the settings brings the total to roughly 170, so I'll need to cut a little more.

Trimming the stool bolts to three and merging them, cutting the settings' cutlery and dividers down, and dropping the grime rings and spills to two each should bring the total near 155.

Still writing the cat's tail as a partial torus, working out how its arc should wrap around the front of the seat.

Still settling the tail's arc, which I'll make a little larger than the paws so it clears them, then I'll start writing the code.

I'm writing the buildShell function and wondering whether Ctx should be defined locally or taken from the module, since a duplicate declaration could conflict. I'm leaning toward typing the destructured parameters inline instead.

Now I'm working out the batch collector: boxes grouped by colour and merged into one part per colour, so the deck grating stays within the 170-part budget.

Still writing the batch helper and merging geometry per colour...

Still sizing the grating and bolts: roughly 108 tiles and about 130 small bolt boxes should keep the mesh well under budget. Still sketching the bulkhead's seams: horizontal strips at four heights on its front face, kept thin so they sit just proud of the surface where the range abuts it.

Now I'm placing the hatch on the bulkhead face: a frame of dark bars around a panel about 0.7 wide and 1.6 tall, with vertical seams set at two depths so the hatch sits between them.

Still placing the hatch's wheel-lock and hinges, plus an amber indicator lamp and bolts around the frame.
